title: Electricity: Current, Voltage, Resistance (KS4 Physics)
subject: Physics
strapline: The three key quantities and Ohm’s law.
facts: Current is the rate of flow of charge, measured in amperes (A) with an ammeter (in series).
Potential difference (voltage) is the energy given to the charge, measured in volts (V) with a voltmeter (in parallel).
Resistance opposes the flow of current, measured in ohms (Ω).
Ohm’s law: voltage = current × resistance (V = I × R).
In a series circuit, current is the same everywhere and the voltages add up.
In a parallel circuit, the voltage is the same across each branch and the currents add up.
Increasing the resistance (for a fixed voltage) decreases the current.

quick_quiz.q: What is the unit of resistance?
How is an ammeter connected in a circuit?

teacher_tips: Anchor ammeter=series, voltmeter=parallel with a quick rule.
Rearrange V = IR fluently in all forms.
Contrast series and parallel rules side by side in a table.
